title: Læringsspill – samtale med barn og unge om vanskelige tema
description: RVTS Øst, en del av stiftelsen Pilar, skal inngå avtale med én leverandør om overføring, videreutvikling og drift av det elektroniske læringsspillet på snakkemedbarn.no. Læringsspillet er avatarbasert og brukes til trening på vanskelige samtaler med barn og unge om blant annet vold, overgrep, psykisk helse, selvskading og selvmordstanker. Målgruppen er ansatte i skole, barnehage, helsestasjon, barnevern, PPT og andre som møter barn og unge i sårbare situasjoner. Anskaffelsen omfatter overføring av eksisterende faglig innhold og datagrunnlag til leverandørens løsning i en etableringsfase, drift, vedlikehold og brukerstøtte, videreutvikling av eksisterende innhold og avatarer, samt utvikling av nye avatarer og scenarioer etter bestilling. Oppdragsgiver legger størst vekt på faglig kvalitet, pedagogisk treffsikkerhet, læringseffekt og kontroll over avatarenes atferd. Innhold og data skal være strukturert og gjenbrukbare uavhengig av leverandør. Avtalen inngås på SSA-L, og anskaffelsen er ikke delt opp i delkontrakter.

buyer: Land Baden-Württemberg, vertreten durch das Ministerium für Wissenschaft, Forschung und Kunst Baden-Württemberg (MWK)
title: Germany – Computer archiving services – Zentrales elektronisches Akten- und Dokumentenmanagementsystem für die BAföG-Ämter (kurz: E-Akte)
description: Das Land Baden-Württemberg, vertreten durch das Ministerium für Wissenschaft, Forschung und Kunst Baden-Württemberg (MWK), möchte ein elektronisches Akten- und Dokumentenmanagementsystem (nachfolgend: E-Akte) für die Bearbeitung von Förderverfahren nach dem Bundesausbildungsförderungsgesetz (BAföG) im Fachverfahren Bafög21 beschaffen und einführen. Zu diesem Zweck schreibt der Auftraggeber eine Rahmenvereinbarung aus, auf deren Grundlage die abrufberechtigten Parteien des Bafög21-Verbunds - das Land Baden-Württemberg, Rheinland-Pfalz und Mecklenburg-Vorpommern - den Auftragnehmer mit der Anbindung und dem Betrieb der E-Akte an das Fachverfahren Bafög21 in den BAföG-Ämtern bei den Studierendenwerken bzw. Hochschulen beauftragen können. Hierdurch können die abrufberechtigten Parteien die Dienstleistung ohne zusätzliches förmliches Vergabeverfahren abrufen. Der Auftraggeber weist darauf hin, dass der Freistaat Sachsen Mitglied des Bafög21-Verbunds ist, aber keine abrufberechtigte Partei der Ausschreibung. Bafög21 bleibt auch nach Anbindung der E-Akte das führende Fachverfahren für die BAföG-Sachbearbeitung. Die E-Akte ergänzt die fachliche Bearbeitung im Fachverfahren Bafög21 durch eine einheitliche, medienbrucharme und nachvollziehbare Aktenführung. Die beteiligten Länder tragen die Kosten der jeweils von ihnen abgerufenen Leistungen des Auftragnehmers selbst. Die beteiligten Länder verfügen über folgende Anzahl an BAföG-Ämtern bei den Studierendenwerken bzw. Hochschulen: - Baden-Württemberg: 8 Studierendenwerke; - Rheinland-Pfalz: 11 Hochschulen; - Mecklenburg-Vorpommern: 2 Studierendenwerke. Der Auftraggeber weist darauf hin, dass die Finanzierung der Anbindung der BAföG-Ämter bei den Studierendenwerken bzw. Hochschulen in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern nicht gesichert ist. Die Rahmenvereinbarung sieht keine Mindestabnahmemenge vor. Der Auftraggeber schätzt die Menge der anzubindenden BAföG-Ämter auf 21. Die Höchstmenge der anzubindenden BAföG-Ämter beträgt 21. Mit Erreichen der Höchstmenge verliert die Rahmenvereinbarung ihre Wirkung.

title: Swanley Park Footpath Refurbishment
description: Swanley Town Council is seeking suitably qualified and experienced contractors to undertake the excavation, removal, reconstruction and improvement of two existing footpaths. The project aims to improve accessibility, durability and the overall quality of the footpath network through the installation of wider, fit-for-purpose pathways that meet the requirements of their intended use. The works will comprise the following: Footpath One Footpath One extends approximately 355.4 linear metres and will broadly follow the alignment of the existing footpath. The pathway will be widened to provide a finished width of approximately 2.5 metres, excluding edging. The construction must be suitable for occasional vehicular access, with the appropriate sub-base and construction specification provided to accommodate this requirement. Footpath Two Footpath Two currently measures approximately 29 linear metres and will be extended to approximately 62.3 linear metres. The completed pathway will provide a finished width of approximately 2 metres, excluding edging, improving the provision and usability of the route. Surfacing Options and Construction Requirements The Council is currently exploring a range of surfacing options for the proposed footpaths, including self-binding gravel, tarmac and block paving. Contractors may be required to consider the suitability, durability, maintenance requirements, accessibility and whole-life costs associated with these options to help inform the Council's final decision on the preferred surfacing materials. The appointed contractor will be expected to undertake the necessary excavation and removal of existing footpath materials, prepare the underlying formation, install an appropriate sub-base and construct the new footpaths in accordance with the agreed specification. The works will also include suitable edging, finishing details and any associated reinstatement required to leave the completed pathways in a safe, stable and serviceable condition. All works must be carried out to an appropriate professional standard, with due consideration given to site conditions, public safety, drainage, accessibility and the long-term performance of the finished surfaces. The contractor will be responsible for ensuring that the construction methods and materials used are suitable for the intended use of each footpath. The Council is seeking a cost-effective and durable solution that provides improved pedestrian routes, meets the operational requirements of the site and offers good long-term value for money. Arrange for a site visit if required by contacting (George) gbrooker@swanleytowncouncil.gov.uk Apply by sending your quote to (Ryan) rhayman@swanleytowncouncil.gov.uk

title: Smoking Cessation Workplace Outreach
description: This tender is being run as a Competitive Process under the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. Smoking remains a leading cause of preventable illness and premature death. Employees in routine and manual occupations in Wolverhampton have a significantly higher smoking prevalence, compared to the general population. The aim of this service is to support to successfully quit smoking through a structured, evidence-based cessation programme. The workplace outreach smoking cessation delivery will recruit staff to deliver evidence-based services for adult smokers working in routine and manual occupations to stop smoking. In local workplaces, the service will provide information, advice, and guidance; self-help tools; and lifestyle interventions to enable Service Users to achieve and maintain positive lifestyle changes.

title: UoD-EFM034-TC-2026 - Water Hygiene Monitoring
description: Estates & Campus Services are required to re-tender the Monitoring, servicing and reactive maintenance contract. We are seeking another reputable Water hygiene monitoring accredited supplier with a proven record of water hygiene monitoring of domestic and commercial domestic water systems. The aims and objectives of this contract are to ensure the continuing safety of staff, student's & visitors of the University and the wider public. This maintenance service is delivered across the University`s Estate comprising the City Centre campus as well as other outlying properties. All properties are located within the Dundee City boundary. These properties include an extensive variety of operational data centre and research facilities, teaching facilities, sport facilities and horticultural facilities. The University believes the Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006 (TUPE) may apply to this contract. Tenderers should allow for the transfer of one (1) staff member currently engaged in delivering the water hygiene operational control regime, subject to confirmation through the procurement process. An anonymised TUPE/Employee Liability Information schedule will be provided separately (where applicable). Tenderers must confirm their approach to TUPE, including mobilisation, management arrangements, and integration of the transferring employee into service delivery.

title: Managed Detection and Response (MDR)
description: Med henblik på at beskytte Statens IT (Ordregiver) mod aktuelle og fremtidige cybertrusler anvender Ordregiver en række sikkerhedsteknologier, herunder en Extended Detection and Response (XDR)-platform. XDR-platformen understøtter indsamling, korrelation og analyse af sikkerhedsrelaterede hændelser på tværs af Ordregivers it-miljø med henblik på at beskytte systemer, tjenester og data samt sikre dataenes fortrolighed, integritet og tilgængelighed. Henset hertil udbyder Ordregiver en kontrakt, hvis formål er at understøtte og styrke Ordregivers egen operative it-sikkerhed gennem levering af en Managed Detection and Response (MDR)-tjeneste fra et Security Operations Center (SOC). MDR-tjenesten skal anvende og supplere Ordregivers XDR-platform med døgnbemandet overvågning, analyse, detektion, validering, eskalering og håndtering af sikkerhedshændelser. Tjenesten skal leveres 24 timer i døgnet, 365 dage om året, og bidrage til hurtig identifikation, vurdering og håndtering af cybertrusler og sikkerhedshændelser. Tjenesteydelserne udgør et væsentligt element i Ordregivers fortsatte modnings- og udviklingsproces på cybersikkerhedsområdet med fokus på teknologi, processer, kompetencer og samarbejde på tværs af interne og eksterne interessenter. Med udbuddet ønsker Ordregiver adgang til en professionel MDR-tjeneste, der kan imødekomme Ordregivers høje krav til kvalitet, robusthed og effektivitet, samt en leverandør, der løbende kan indgå i dialog med Ordregiver om udviklingen inden for cybersikkerhed, herunder trusselsbilledet, teknologiske muligheder, automatisering, kompetenceudvikling og løbende forbedringer af sikkerhedsniveauet. Leverandøren skal gennemføre en teknisk, organisatorisk og processuel Transition Ind, der sikrer, at de løbende MDR-ydelser kan leveres fra overgang til driftsfasen. Ordregiver gør opmærksom på, at Ordregiver har indgået kontrakt med to (2) leverandører til varetagelse af Ordregivers eksisterende XDR-platform, som leverandøren skal samarbejde med i forbindelse med Transition Ind. Som led heri skal leverandøren etablere og konfigurere de nødvendige integrationer mellem Ordregivers XDR-platform og øvrige relevante sikkerhedskilder samt leverandørens værktøjer og platforme, der anvendes til kontraktens opfyldelse. Leverandøren skal levere Løbende MDR-ydelser; herunder kontinuerlig overvågning, analyse, korrelation, validering og detektion af alarmer og sikkerhedshændelser. Leverandøren skal foretage triagering og kvalificering af alarmer med henblik på at identificere reelle sikkerhedshændelser samt sikre rettidig eskalering og advisering i overensstemmelse med aftalte processer og serviceniveauer. Disse løbende MDR-ydelser omfatter herunder: • Kontinuerlig SOC-overvågning af sikkerhedsrelaterede hændelser og alarmer. • Analyse, korrelation og kvalificering af hændelser på tværs af relevante datakilder. • Identifikation, detektion og validering af sikkerhedshændelser. • Udarbejdelse, implementering og løbende optimering af detektionsregler, use cases og analysemodeller. • Anvendelse af relevant Threat Intelligence til understøttelse af detektions- og analysearbejdet. • Løbende vurdering af trusselsbilledet og dets relevans for Ordregivers miljø. • Proaktiv identifikation af potentielle sikkerhedshændelser og sikkerhedsrisici, herunder gennem Threat Hunting-aktiviteter. • Eskalering, advisering og rapportering af sikkerhedshændelser i henhold til aftalte processer og serviceniveauer. • Vedligeholdelse af eksisterende integrationer samt etablering af nye integrationer efter behov. • Optimering og videreudvikling af Ordregivers XDR-platform og øvrige sikkerhedsløsninger. • Rådgivning vedrørende udvikling og modning af Ordregivers sikkerhedsorganisation, sikkerhedsprocesser og governance. • Gennemførelse af målrettede Threat Hunting-forløb og analyser af mistænkelige aktiviteter. • Incident Response-bistand ved sikkerhedshændelser efter rekvisition fra Ordregiver, herunder analyse, afgrænsning, håndtering, afhjælpning og genopretning. • Bistand ved større sikkerhedshændelser, cyberkriser og koordination med relevante interessenter. • Sikkerhedsfaglig rådgivning og strategisk sparring om udviklingen inden for cybersikkerhed. Kontrakten omfatter desuden tværgående ydelser, herunder dokumentation, rapportering, governance, kvalitetssikring og informationssikkerhed, der leveres gennem hele kontraktperioden. Endvidere omfatter kontrakten forpligtelser ved kontraktophør (Transition Ud), der skal sikre en kontrolleret, sikker og dokumenteret overdragelse af viden, data, processer, integrationer og øvrige kontraktrelaterede leverancer til Ordregiver eller en efterfølgende leverandør.

title: Belgium – Market research services – Mystery Shopping
description: La SNCB souhaite conclure un accord-cadre relatif à la réalisation de prestations de mystery shopping visant à mesurer, suivre et améliorer la qualité de service délivrée aux voyageurs au sein de son réseau ferroviaire. L'objectif du marché est d'évaluer de manière indépendante et objective l'expérience client aux différents points de contact entre les voyageurs et les collaborateurs ou partenaires de la SNCB. Les observations réalisées devront notamment permettre d'analyser la qualité de l'accueil, le professionnalisme, la disponibilité, la qualité des informations fournies ainsi que le respect des standards de service définis par la SNCB. Le marché comprend entre autres la préparation des campagnes de mystery shopping, le recrutement et la gestion des mystery shoppers, l'organisation et le suivi du travail de terrain, la collecte et la validation des données, ainsi que la production des rapports et analyses destinés à la SNCB.

title: Belgium – Scheduling software package – IT-applicatie voor twee doeleinden: “scheduling” en “dispatching”
description: Dans le cadre d'un programme de transformation pluriannuel nommé shERPa, la SNCB migrera son paysage SAP ECC actuel vers la solution SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud Edition (PCE), ainsi que vers plusieurs solutions SaaS de SAP (IBP, APM, C4C) selon une approche greenfield. / Au sein de ce programme de transformation, plusieurs projets ont été définis autour des solutions SAP pour la direction B-Technics de la SNCB, dans le cadre de la maintenance et des révisions des trains. Pour le projet (Centre de Compétence), le projet (Atelier de Traction Pilote) et le projet (Révision), il existe un besoin pour une solution de planification et de répartition (scheduling & dispatching) permettant de distribuer et d'attribuer les ordres de travail et les tâches (provenant de SAP Plant Maintenance, SAP Production Planning et éventuellement SAP Project Systems). / La solution doit être capable de planifier et de répartir de manière flexible les ordres de maintenance SAP via un tableau de planification graphique. La planification (scheduling) détermine le moment où les ordres et leurs opérations sont exécutés, en tenant compte de la capacité, des matériaux, des statuts, des échéances, des dépendances et des arrêts de maintenance. La répartition (dispatching) détermine qui exécute quelles opérations, en tenant compte de la disponibilité et des qualifications des techniciens, des conflits, de l'avancement et du taux d'occupation. La solution doit s'intégrer de manière fluide avec SAP S/4HANA et répondre aux exigences en matière de sécurité, de SSO, d'autorisations et de performance.

title: Actuarial Costing and Return on Investment Analysis for the Modernization of the Federal Workers’ Compensation Regime
description: The purpose of this requirement is to obtain an independent actuarial costing analysis of the short-, medium- and long-term direct and indirect costs if the current federal workers’ compensation regime remains unchanged, or if two options for modernizing the regime are implemented. The analysis must include both overall costs of the regime, and costs for (a) the five federal employers with the highest volumes of workers’ compensation claims and (b) a selection of federal employers with moderate claim volumes. The analysis should also provide a return on investment (ROI) for the two modernization options.

title: APN - NORAD Northern Basing Infrastructure (NNBI), NWT
description: Advance Procurement Notice NORAD Northern Basing Infrastructure (NNBI) Forward Operating Locations (FOL) Inuvik and Yellowknife (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation. This is an advance notice of potential contracts with anticipated security requirements, providing interested design-builders with an opportunity to begin the sponsorship request process for potentially obtaining the required security clearance(s) that are anticipated. Note that there is no guarantee that these solicitations will proceed or that any security clearance(s) will be granted under the sponsorship process in a timely fashion or otherwise. Description of the Program and Services The Department of National Defence (DND) is investing in infrastructure developments for the North American Aerospace Defence Command (NORAD) Modernization and Continental Defence at the FOLs in Inuvik and Yellowknife, Northwest Territories. This infrastructure investment aims to ensure that the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) have the tools they need to achieve their security and sovereignty objectives. These improvements will enable advanced aircraft operations and quick mobilization in the North for NORAD missions. The infrastructure requirements for the Inuvik and Yellowknife FOLs will include the following but are not limited to: Airfield improvements; New and/or repurposed hangars with aprons and taxiways; Ammunition compounds; Fuel facilities; Accommodations, warehousing, planning, multi-purpose facilities, and support equipment; Robust IT, Cyber, and Logistics infrastructure.  Preliminary rough order of magnitude (ROM) estimates for the various facility components for each locations are as follows, subject to revision: Total hangar space, ~ 33,000 m2 Fuel storage, between 500,000  to 2,000,000 litres Office space  500 m2 Ammunition Storage 600 m2 Accommodations 4,000 m2 Fire Hall 2,000 m2 Multi-purpose facilities 9,000 m2 Indoor storage (Total), 9,000 m2 Apron 122,000 m2 Total asphalt surface 72,000 m2 The delivery method for this infrastructure will be Modified Design-Build (MDB) contracts, with one MDB contract per site and an estimated total contract value that may exceed $5B for each location. These multi-year contracts consist of the following sequential and/or concurrent phases and are not limited to: Requirements validation, concept development, market analysis and planning activities. Design Phase activities. Construction Phase activities. It is anticipated that the Request for Proposal (RFP) will include detailed evaluation criteria; however, these remain subject to change and will be finalized and fully described in the RFP documentation upon release. At a high level, it is expected that the RFP will assess proponents on demonstrated experience across a range of factors, including northern design and construction experience, experience delivering similar asset types (both within and outside of northern environments), and the integration of design and construction capabilities within a single team. Key personnel requirements will include demonstrated northern experience for certain roles. The evaluation of approach and methodology is expected to consider how proponents plan to successfully deliver projects in northern environments, including logistics, climate, and constructability considerations, as well as their approach to Indigenous participation based on principles of meaningful participation and mitigation of potential adverse effects. In addition to the technical evaluation, a formal interview process will be conducted to further assess team capability to successfully deliver the project in a northern environment. The terms and conditions of the contract will allow for self-performed work by the design-build team.  The MDB solicitation for Inuvik is projected to be released in Fall 2026 and Yellowknife in Summer 2027. This is conditional on receiving approval to proceed by DND. The Government of Canada is committed to advancing reconciliation and fostering meaningful engagement with Indigenous Peoples. In support of these commitments, DND aims to create opportunities for Indigenous businesses and communities through meaningful subcontracting, employment, and training related to the proposed project. To align with these objectives, the successful proponents will be required to develop an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP) as part of the MDB contracts. The IBPs will outline proposed initiatives and opportunities for Indigenous participation, including subcontracting, employment, and training activities. Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the tender documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Facility Security Clearance at the level of SECRET. Industrial Security Program (ISP) Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing design-builders early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, design-builders that intend to submit a proposal on one or more of these projects and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, design-builders are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (Project number on the MERX notice); Contract number PR24NNBI; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored for. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the design-builders to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a design-builder: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation (s) (Contract number(s) listed on their request for sponsorship) being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package, and has submitted a proposal. DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Antoine am Rhyn Regional Service Line Leader, Contract Services Defence Construction Canada 819-431-7650 Antoine.amrhyn@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process and does not provide any representations or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) b

title: APN - Facilities Maintenance and Support Services Northern Canada
description: Advance Procurement Notice Facilities Maintenance and Support Services Northern Canada (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. Note that there is no guarantee that these solicitation(s) will proceed or that any security clearance(s) will be granted under the sponsorship process in a timely fashion or otherwise. Description of the Project and Services The Department of National Defence requires Facilities Maintenance and Support Services for approximately 100 existing buildings and associated utility infrastructure with an approximate total gross floor area of 60,000 m2. In addition to the buildings there are utility services, parking lots, sidewalks, roads and landscaped areas that form part of the site included under the provisions of the project(s). The site locations are as follows: Manitoba: Churchill Northwest Territories: Inuvik, Yellowknife Yukon: Whitehorse Nunavut: Eureka, Resolute Bay, Gascoyne Inlet, Nanisivik Naval Facility, Rankin Inlet, Iqaluit, The services provided by the Contractor may vary based on Sites: All the services listed will have Scheduled and/or “On-Demand" requirements. Hard Services Building Envelope Maintenance Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning & Refrigeration Systems Door Systems Electrical Systems Elevator and Lifting Systems Plumbing Systems Fire Detection and Suppression Systems Generators Life Safety Systems Security and Access Control Systems Kitchen Appliances and Equipment Soft Services Integrated Pest Management Services Landscaping and Grounds Maintenance Services Janitorial Services Hazardous Waste Management Services Environmental Services Snow and Ice Control Services Solid Waste Management Utility Billing Support Services Facilities Support Services Service Management & Coordination Maintenance Program Management Emergency Readiness and Response Asset Investment Advice Help Desk Services The Contractor(s) will also be required to undertake work that is outside the scope of the scheduled and demand services. This work will be priced, managed and implemented using an Additional Work Request (AWR) process. The services will be delivered through Facility Maintenance and Support Services (FM) contracts. title: Zajištění realizace jazykových kurzů anglického jazyka pro zaměstnance ČIŽP v letech 2027-2030
description: Předmětem plnění této veřejné zakázky je poskytování jazykových skupinových kurzů anglického jazyka pro zaměstnance zadavatele s intenzitou jedné vyučovací hodiny týdně a individuálních studijních plánů anglického jazyka se stejnou frekvencí. Vyučovací hodinou se rozumí 90 minut nepřetržité výuky bez přestávky. Jedná se o kurzy obecného jazyka, které budou dodavatelem poskytovány přednostně prezenčně v prostorách zadavatele a v prostorách oblastních inspektorátů a poboček zadavatele. Pouze v mimořádných případech a na základě písemné žádosti zadavatele lze službu poskytnout i online. Cílem výuky je praktické využití anglického jazyka v pracovních situacích, s důrazem na rozvoj komunikačních dovedností. Výuka bude přizpůsobena specifickým potřebám zaměstnanců České inspekce životního prostředí, včetně odborné terminologie (např. environmentální témata).

title: Harrastamisen Mäntsälän malli 2025-2027 (DPS)
description: Harrastamisen Mäntsälän malli on osa valtakunnallista opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriön tukemaa Harrastamisen Suomen mallia, jonka tavoitteena on tarjota peruskoululaisille (vuosiluokkien 1-9 oppilaat) laadukkaita, mieluisia ja maksuttomia harrastusmahdollisuuksia oman koulun ja kodin läheisyydessä, koulupäivän yhteydessä, lasten ja nuorten toiveita kuullen. Harrastuksen järjestäjinä voivat olla urheiluseurat, kulttuuritoimijat, nuorisojärjestöt, kunnat, yritykset ja muut harrastustoimintaa järjestävät yhteisöt. Harrastustoiminnan tulee olla säännöllistä, viikoittaista ja laadukasta koko lukuvuoden kestävää toimintaa, joka alkaa elokuussa ja loppuu toukokuussa. Harrastustoimintaa ei voi järjestää etänä (poikkeuksena vuosiluokkien 7-9 oppilaille suunnattu digitaalinen harrastustoiminta), vaan se tulee toteuttaa paikan päällä ja paikalla on aina oltava valvoja. Ohjaajan osaamisen tulee olla riittävä laadukkaan avoimen toiminnan järjestämiseen. Harrastusten ohjaajien tulee olla täysi-ikäisiä ja ammattimaisia omalla osaamisalueellaan sekä omata kokemusta lasten ja nuorten parissa toimimisesta. Apuohjaaja voi olla alaikäinen. Mäntsälän kunta kilpailuttaa lapsille ja nuorille suunnatun harrastustoiminnan järjestämisen aikajaksolle elokuu 2025 – toukokuu 2027. Kilpailutukset toteutetaan nyt perustettavan dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän (DPS) puitteissa kaksivaiheisesti ja sen toteutuminen on ehdollinen myönnetylle valtionavustukselle. Ensimmäisessä vaiheessa dynaamisessa hankintajärjestelmässä harrastuksen järjestäjät ilmoittautuvat mukaan järjestelmään, jolloin tarkistetaan ehdokkaan soveltuvuus. Kaikki kelpoisuus- ja vähimmäisvaatimukset täyttävät tarjoajat valitaan mukaan dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään. Osallistumishakemuksen yhteydessä ei tarjota hintoja. Dynaamisessa hankintajärjestelmässä kaikki kiinnostuneet toimittajat voivat pyytää osallistua osallistumisilmoituksen määräaikaan 30.11.2026 asti. Toisessa vaiheessa ehdokkaat voivat antaa tarjouksia tarjouskilpailuihin, jotka järjestetään dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän sisällä. Tarjouspyyntöjä lähetetään toimittajarekisteriin hyväksytyille tarjoajille. Tarjouksia tullaan pyytämään seuraavista osa-alueista: 1) liikunnallinen, 2) kulttuurinen ja käden taidot sekä 3) digitaalinen harrastustoiminta. Näiden osa-alueiden sisällä tullaan järjestämään tarjouspyyntöjä lukuvuosittain tai tarvittaessa lukukausittain dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän voimassa olon ajan. Tulevan lukuvuoden 2025-2026 harrastustoiminnan kilpailutuksen tavoiteaikataulun mukaan tulemme pyytämään tähän dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään hyväksytyiltä ehdokkailta tarjouksia kevään 2025 aikana 8.5.2025 saakka, kerhotoiminta alkaa elokuussa 2025. Tarkistamme mahdolliset muutostarpeet kevätlukukaudelle joulukuun aikana. Seuraavan lukuvuoden 2026-2027 harrastustarjonnan kokoaminen aloitetaan mukaan ilmoittautuneiden toimijoiden kanssa toukokuun 2026 aikana. Toimijaksi voi ilmoittautua ympäri vuoden. Osallistumishakemuksia käsitellään ensimmäisen kerran viikolla 13/2025 ja jatkossa vähintään puolivuosittain huhti- ja joulukuussa ennen uuden lukukauden alkua ja ennen tarjouspyyntöjen lähettämistä. Liikunnallinen harrastustoiminta Kilpailutus toteutetaan dynaamisena kilpailutuksena kaksivaiheisesti. Ensimmäisessä vaiheessa dynaamisessa hankintajärjestelmässä (DPS) harrastuksen järjestäjät ilmoittautuvat mukaan ko. järjestelmään. Tässä yhteydessä tarkistetaan ehdokkaan soveltuvuus. Kaikki kelpoisuus- ja vähimmäisvaatimukset täyttävät toimittajat valitaan mukaan DPS:ään. Toisessa vaiheessa ehdokkaat voivat antaa tarjouksia tarjouskilpailuihin, jotka järjestetään DPS:n sisällä. title: Sairaalasänkyjen, sairaalakalusteiden ja lääkekaappien hankinta
description: Hankinnan kohteena ovat sairaalasänkyjen, sairaalakalusteiden sekä lääkekaappien hankinnat Vantaan ja Keravan hyvinvointialueelle tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisin ehdoin. Hankinta on jaettu kuuteen (6) osa-alueeseen: Osa-alue 1. Sairaalasängyt ja potilaspöydät Osa-alue 2. Tutkimus- ja toimenpidepöydät Osa-alue 3. Lääkekaapit ja lääkejääkaapit Osa-alue 4. Muut sairaalakalusteet ja tarvikkeet Osa-alue 5. Gynekologiset tutkimuspöydät Osa-alue 6. Vaunut ja logistiikkakalusteet Tarjoaja voi tarjota yhteen tai useampaan osa-alueeseen. Hankinnassa muodostetaan osa-aluekohtaisesti puitejärjestely, johon valitaan kaksi (2) Toimittajaa per osa-alue, mikäli tarjouspyynnön ehdot täyttäviä tarjouksia on saatu vähintään ilmoitettu määrä. Toimittajat asetetaan osa-aluekohtaisesti kokonaistaloudellisen edullisuuden perusteella etusijajärjestykseen. Osa-alueissa 2, 4 ja 6, mikäli osa-aluekohtaisesti kahden etusijajärjestyksessä parhaiten sijoittuneen tarjoajan tuotetarjonnat eivät yhdessä kata kaikkia kyseisen osa-alueen tarjouspyynnössä määriteltyjä tuotepositioita, hankintayksikkö valitsee osa-aluekohtaiseen puitejärjestelyyn myös kolmanneksi sijoittuneen tarjouspyynnön ehdot täyttäneen tarjoajan tarjouksen tuotepositioiden saatavuuden varmistamiseksi. Osa-alueeseen valitaan kuitenkin enintään kolme (3) toimittajaa. Sopimuskausi on määräaikaisena voimassa kaksi (2) vuotta. Tavoitteena on, että sopimuskausi alkaa 1.1.2027. Osa-aluekohtaiseen puitesopimukseen sisältyy optiona puitesopimuksen jatkaminen enintään kahdella (2) vuodella. Sopimusehdot ovat optiokaudella tämän puitesopimuksen mukaiset. Hankinnan ennakoitu kokonaisarvo neljän (4) vuoden sopimuskaudelle on noin 900 000 - 1,1 miljoonaa euroa (alv 0 %). Tarkempi erittely hankinnan kohteesta on kohdassa Hankinnan kohteen kriteerit. Tarjoajan tulee antaa hinta positioihin 1.1-1.3. Optiona hankittavien tuotteiden hinnat eivät vaikuta vertailuhintaan., Muut sairaalakalusteet ja tarvikkeet Hankinnan kohteena ovat muut sairaalakalusteet. Tarkempi erittely hankinnan kohteesta on kohdassa Hankinnan kohteen kriteerit. Tarkempi erittely hankinnan kohteesta on kohdassa Hankinnan kohteen kriteerit. Tarjoajan tulee tarjota vähintään neljää (4) osa-alueen tuotetta. Tarjoaja voi jättää enintään yhden (1) tuotteen tarjoamatta. Tarjouspalvelussa tulee valita valikosta tuotteet, jotka Tarjoaja haluaa tarjota, ja jättää valitsematta tuotteen, jota ei tarjota. title: Kajaanin rauniolinnan pohjoisen ja eteläisen siipilinnakkeiden muurin ja muurinharjojen korjausurakka
description: Metsähallitus kilpailuttaa Kajaanin rauniolinnan muurin ja muurinharjojen korjausurakan tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteenä olevien suunnitelmien mukaisesti. Hankinta sisältää kaikki työt ja materiaalit sekä kuljetuskustannukset, jotka työn toteuttaminen edellyttää. Urakkamuoto molemmilla osa-alueilla on kokonaishintaurakka ja urakassa noudatetaan rakennusurakan yleisiä sopimusehtoja YSE 1998 (RT 16–10660) sopimusluonnokseen ja urakkaohjelmaan määritetyillä tarkennuksilla. Pääurakoitsija toimii kohteen päätoteuttajana ja vastaa päätoteuttajan velvollisuuksista (YSE 1 § - 4 §) mm. työturvallisuudesta ja yleisistä työmaavelvoitteista. Päätoteuttaja vastaa tarvittavista työmaapalveluista, jos tarjouspyynnössä tai sen liitteenä olevassa aineistossa ei ole muuta mainittu. Hankinta on jaettu osa-alueisiin: 1. Pohjoinen siipilinnake N 2. Eteläinen siipilinnake P Tarjoajan on tarjottava molempia osa-alueita. Hankintayksikkö voi harkintansa mukaan tai budjettisyistä toteuttaa vain toisen osa-alueista. Toimittajaksi valitaan toteutettavan urakan halvimman tarjouksen tehnyt soveltuvuusvaatimukset täyttävä tarjoaja. Työkokonaisuus, materiaalit ja laajuus on esitetty seikkaperäisemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteenä olevissa suunnitelma-aineistoissa ja urakkarajaliitteessä. Tarjoaja toimii pääurakoitsijana ja lainsäädännön tarkoittamana päätoteuttajana. Urakoitsijan velvollisuuksiin kuuluvat kaikki päätoteuttajan velvollisuudet. Urakoitsijan on huolehdittava siitä, että kaikki urakoitsijan tähän työmaahan liittyvät työturvallisuusvelvoitteet ja erityisesti Valtioneuvoston asetus rakennustyön turvallisuudesta 205/2009 mukaiset rakennustyön turvallisuutta koskevat määräykset tulevat noudatetuiksi. Tätä työkokonaisuutta varten tehty työmaan työturvallisuusasiakirja on tarjouspyynnön liitteenä 6. Tarjoajan tulee tutustua huolellisesti tarjouspyyntöaineistoon ja sen liitteisiin ennen tarjouksen jättämistä. Tarjous tulee jättää 30.11.2026 kello 16.00 mennessä. Määräajan jälkeen saapuneita tarjouksia ei huomioida. Työt voidaan aloittaa 10.5.2027. Sopimus allekirjoitetaan lähtökohtaisesti sähköisesti. Töiden tulee olla valmiit ja tilaajan vastaanotettavissa 30.9.2027 kello 16.00. Urakoitsija voi määrittää urakan aloitusajankohdan vapaasti, mutta työt tulee suorittaa yhtäjaksoisesti loppuun urakan käynnistyttyä. Urakan tarkasta toteutusajankohdasta sovitaan sopimuksen selonottoneuvotteluiden yhteydessä. Tarjoajan oletetaan esittävän aikataulua urakalle neuvotteluiden yhteydessä. Kohteen poikkeuksellisen voimakkaan suojeluarvon vuoksi työn laadukasta toteutusta valvotaan erityisen tarkasti. Tilaaja varaa oikeuden järjestää työmaalle kameravalvonnan omaisuuden suojaamiseksi ja/tai tuotantoprosessien asianmukaisen toiminnan valvomiseksi sekä turvallisuutta, omaisuutta ja/tai tuotantoprosessia vaarantavien tilanteiden ennaltaehkäisemiseksi tai selvittämiseksi., Pohjoinen siipilinnake N Kajaanin rauniolinnan pohjoisen siipilinnakkeiden muurin ja muurinharjojen korjausurakka tämän tarjouspyynnön sekä liitteenä olevan aineiston mukaisesti., Eteläinen siipilinnake P Kajaanin rauniolinnan eteläisen siipilinnakkeiden muurin ja muurinharjojen korjausurakka tämän tarjouspyynnön sekä liitteenä olevan aineiston mukaisesti.,

title: Quantum Benchmarking Initiative Topic (QBIT) Stage A
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is issuing a Quantum Benchmarking Initiative topic (QBIT) to solicit innovative approaches addressing challenges related to quantum computing. The QBIT will examine approaches to constructing a utility-scale fault-tolerant quantum computer and computational workflows that include quantum compute steps. Proposed research should investigate approaches that enable revolutionary advances in design, engineering, testing, and evaluation of such systems. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice. The purpose of this QBIT is to encourage new entrants to QBI, ensuring DARPA has visibility into all approaches and potential solutions. While this QBIT is not intended to solicit proposals from performers selected under prior QBI or US2QC solicitations, those performers are not precluded from submitting new proposals under this PA if they believe their approach offers new or distinct contributions to the QBI initiative. This QBIT is issued under DARPA�s Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI), described in the QBI 2026 Program Announcement (PA), DARPA-PA-26-02. To view the original DARPA PA for QBI 2026, visit SAM.gov under solicitation number DARPA-PA-26-02: https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/c26b38bf041a4d70b00ed619bebb4773/view

title: Q301--Biodesix, Inc. (621 II) (PENDING PROPOSAL)
description: Revised Language SCOPE OF SOLICITATION The Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) program is also known as the GSA Schedules Program or the Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) Program. The FSS program is directed and managed by GSA and provides Federal agencies with a simplified process for obtaining commercial supplies and services at prices associated with volume buying. Indefinite-delivery, indefinite quantity contracts are awarded to provide supplies and services at stated prices for given periods of time. GSA has delegated authority to the VA to manage the Schedules for medical supplies under the VA FSS program. This solicitation is for the offering of reference laboratory services for the purpose of providing medical laboratory testing for the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of a disease or condition and to assess patient health to make clinical decisions for patient care.� This solicitation is not for facilities that only collect and/or prepare specimens nor for those facilities that only serve as a mailing service and do not perform testing services. This solicitation is issued to establish contracts which may be used on a nonmandatory basis by eligible users, as a source of supply for the supplies or services described herein, for domestic. Domestic delivery is defined as delivery within the 48 contiguous states, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Washington, DC, and U.S. territories . Offerors may be limited to geographic service areas based upon licensing requirements or may offer nationwide delivery. This solicitation further requires that offered prices cover delivery to destinations (i.e. F.O.B. destination) located within the 48 contiguous states and the District of Columbia. Offerors can choose whether or not prices cover delivery f.o.b. destination to Alaska, Hawaii, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Additionally, the solicitation defines the number of calendar days after receipt of order (ARO) within which delivery must be made. Offerors who cannot provide the required minimum geographic coverage, that is one state, will not be considered for award. As specified in the solicitation, offerors shall comply with all state, federal and local regulations, licenses, permits, and accreditation necessary to manage and conduct preanalytic specimen testing services. Offerors must comply with states that require out of state licenses/permits. Therefore, laboratories conducting clinical testing on specimens originating in a state that requires an out of state license/permit must hold that state s Department of Health (or other governing body) clinical laboratory permit, licenses, etc. � Offerors that are not compliant with the originating state s licensing and/or permit requirement, regardless of location, will not be considered for an award for that specific state. Offerors may not subcontract to another laboratory to circumvent the originating state s requirement for licensing, permits, etc. The offeror, in itself, is required to meet the requirements of the solicitation without the aid of a subcontractor. The Government retains sole discretion to determine the offeror s capability, compliance, and to limit SINs or geographic coverage. Commercial Items Per GSA regulations at 538.271(a), MAS awards are for commercial items as defined in FAR 2.101. Special Item Numbers (SINs): FSS solicitations set forth broad categories of accepted products/services, referred to as Special Item Numbers (SINs), listed in the Continuation of SF1449 in Vendor Response Document 02. Offerors are not required to submit their entire catalog of products/services but are free to choose which items they will offer as long as those items fall within one of the solicitation s pre-defined SIN categories. Items that do not fall within one of these SINs are considered to be out of scope of the solicitation and cannot be awarded. An item s acceptability under the schedule may be further restricted by a determination of fair and reasonable pricing. Offered diagnostic testing services must be categorized under the accepted services referenced under the Special Item Numbers (SINs) and classified as a specialties or subspecialties of tests as defined under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA). Please note that items offered are further restricted to those tests with CPT codes. Additionally, FSS will not award any home diagnostic tests under this schedule. Home diagnostic tests/test kits may be proposed under Schedule 65 V II Invitro Diagnostics, Reagents, Test Kits and Test Sets. FDA Regulatory Requirements Reagents used to perform the tests must be FDA cleared, as appropriate, or be identified as a Laboratory Developed Test (LDT). Offerors of tests not in compliance with these requirements shall not be considered for award under this solicitation. New Items vs. Refurbished or Grey Market Goods This solicitation is for the award of new items only. The Contractor shall provide only new equipment and new parts for the required products described herein. Absolutely no grey market goods or refurbished products shall be provided under any delivery order. Grey market goods are defined as genuine branded goods sold outside of an authorized sales-territory (or by non-authorized dealers in an authorized territory) at prices lower than being charged in authorized sales territories (or by authorized dealers). All equipment must be covered by the manufacturer s warranty. Trade Agreements Act The Trade Agreements Act is applicable to all Schedules. In exercising its authority under FAR Part 25, Foreign Acquisition, purchases by Ordering Activities are restricted to either U.S.-made or designated country end products as defined in clause FAR 52.225-5. For the purposes of this services schedule, origin is determined by the country in which the firm providing the service is established, not the location at which the services are performed. Notice of Additional Requirements - Ordering Level In addition to the terms and conditions set forth in this solicitation, the contractor may, in the performance of orders issued under this contract, be responsible for further requirements at the ordering level. For more information on these potential, additional requirements, please see the note in Solicitation Document 01 after FAR clause 52.216-18 Ordering. Please note that the VA does not promote the use of any company s specific Schedule contract. Vendors should be aware that obtaining a VA Schedule contract is not a guarantee of sales. Vendors awarded a VA Schedule contract will need to market their supplies and services to Government customers as they would to commercial customers. A listing of eligible schedule users can be found at on GSA s website at http://gsa.federalschedules.com/resources/eligible-gsa-schedule-users/. title: Q702--Santa Maria IOTA
description: Department of Veterans Affairs Veterans Health Administration Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) October 13, 2026 PRESOLICITATION NOTICE Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation Services in support of the Santa Maria, CA OPC 100% SDVOSB SET ASIDE This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice that the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) intends to solicit quotes to provide non-personal Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation (IOT&A) services for the Santa Maria Outpatient Clinic (OPC). This requirement supports VHA's mission by providing contractor support services to help bring the hospital into full planned operations that will provide health care services to Veterans. This will be a firm-fixed-price contract with an estimated Period of Performance of 31-months. VHA authorized a 28,656 net usable square foot (NUSF) outpatient clinic (OPC) lease project in Santa Maria, California. The project will support the parent facility, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System. The new OPC will replace the existing clinic in Santa Maria, which currently contains 28,612 NUSF. The new clinic will be able to accommodate future workload, provide ample parking (200 spaces), and will adequately support all services in a modern, efficient space. The new clinic will provide all the services offered at the existing clinic, including Primary Care, Mental Health, Audiology, Eye Clinic, Dental, Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, Pathology and Blood Draw, Logistics, Telehealth, Business Office, Community Engagement and Reintegration, and Women's Health. This new facility is essential to accommodate the current demand of 6,634 Unique Santa Maria Veterans and the future potential demand of 7,500 Santa Maria catchment Enrollees The scope includes project support for planning, activating, outfitting, and transitioning the staff and Veterans/patients associated with the project. The scope of services includes Comprehensive Project Management, Comprehensive Interior Design, FF&E, and Space Planning Support; CONOPS and Transitioning Planning; Acquisition Support Services to include package development, Activation, Delivery, Relocation and Installation, Training, and Turnover and Post Occupancy Support for the identified project. This requirement will be set-aside 100% for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) using FAR Part 12 and 37. To be eligible for an SDVOSB set aside under VA s Veterans First Contracting Program, SDVOSBs must: be verified by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) as SDVOSB (see https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ for details) and meet the small business size standard for NAICS 541614. The solicitation is anticipated to be posted on Contract Opportunities for download on or about 30 October 2026. Potential offerors are advised that there may be truncated response time on the solicitation that will follow this Pre-Solicitation notice. Anticipated closing date of the solicitation will be 30 November 2026. Solicitation initial posting date and the closing date are subject to change as necessary. Any questions for this Pre-solicitation notice should be sent via e-mail to both Katherine.Johnson6@va.gov and Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov. No telephone requests/questions will be accepted. This Pre-Solicitation notice does not constitute a request for proposals. P.O.C: Katherine.Johnson@va.gov, Contract Specialist and Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov, Contracting Officer

title: Request for Information/Market Intelligence Notice: Repair Electrical Distribution System Switchgear Stations & Addition of Redundancy Cable Use of Progressive Design Build (PDB) with Other Transaction Authority (OTA)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE: This is a request for information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a solicitation or a request for proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS CODE: 238210 Electrical Contractors and Other Wiring Installation Contractors SMALL BUSINESS STANDARD: $19,000,000.00 NOTE: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base. PROGRAM/PROJECT OVERVIEW: The 11th Contracting Squadron (11 CONS), District of Washington, has a requirement to execute the design-build upgrades, repairs, and/or replacements to the deteriorated Electrical Switching Stations located at B18 and B168 on Joint Base Anacostia Bolling (JBAB) that includes developing a solution to establish a connection by high voltage electrical redundancy cable. The Government is evaluating the feasibility of executing these requirements via Progressive Design-Build (PDB) utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. This project summary establishes the operational requirements, technical baseline, and acquisition framework for the Progressive Design-Build (PDB) Other Transaction Authority (OTA) effort to modernize Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling�s (JBAB) primary electrical infrastructure. Project Title JBAB Electrical Switching Stations (ESS B18 & B168) Modernization & Grid Redundancy Location Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling (JBAB), 11th Wing Acquisition Strategy Progressive Design-Build (PDB) via Other Transaction Authority (OTA) Primary Objective Engineer comprehensive design packages to repair, upgrade, and interconnect deteriorated electrical switching infrastructure Primary Deliverables 100% executable design packages, specifications, and implementation schedules for ESS upgrades, facility hardening, cable routing, and smart-grid wireless SCADA/telemetry Scope Breakdown by Facility & Component ESS B18 (Switching Station Upgrade) � Full replacement of legacy switchgear with FR3 fluid, air-insulated switchgear (per latest UFC 3-550-01) � Life-cycle cost and sustainability integration (UFC 1-200-02) � Thermal partition separating switchgear room from power generation bay � Dedicated HVAC system and air conditioning ductwork � Sized space heating units � High-efficiency interior LED lighting ESS B168 (Repair, Upgrade & Hardening) � Complete switchgear replacement mirroring ESS B168b using FR3 air-insulated switchgear (UFC 3-550-01) � Sustainable design practices (UFC 1-200-02) � Dedicated single HVAC unit and duct system � Interior/exterior high-efficiency LED flood/task lighting � Raised roof profile with comprehensive crack sealing/insulation � Foundation pillar repairs, crawl space waterproofing, and rainwater gutter system � Motorized roll-up door, cyber/physical cypher-locked access doors, and motorized loading dock ramp with widened sidewalk High-Voltage Redundancy Cables � Design 4-circuit bidirectional interconnect (8 cables total) connecting ESS B18 and ESS B168 � Baseline routing derived from 2025 Engineering Study � Mandatory underground routing preference across base footprint � Aerial routing permitted strictly as secondary exception where subsurface obstructions prevent underground installation Wireless SCADA & Grid Telemetry � Air Force long-term smart-grid wireless connectivity architecture � Cell-enabled control panels reporting directly to electric shop web interface without physical comm trunk lines � Relay-to-control panel comm wiring for ESS B18 and ESS B168 � Additional telemetry control panel integrated into ESS B4505 (sub-station to B18) to monitor sub-station power load profiles Key Technical Standards & Compliance Baseline UFC 3-550-01 Exterior Electrical Power Distribution Mandates modern FR3 biodegradable, fire-resistant fluid dielectric air-insulated switchgears, significantly mitigating environmental and thermal hazards. UFC 1-200-02 High Performance and Sustainable Building Requirements Governs energy efficiency, life-cycle cost effectiveness, indoor environmental quality, and durable materials integration. PDB / OTA Authority Prototype / Collaboration Framework Fosters early contractor involvement during Phase 1 design, mitigating unforeseen site and subsurface risk prior to Phase 2 construction commitment. INFORMATION REQUESTED: Interested industry partners are requested to respond to the following questions to help shape the final acquisition strategy: Company Profile: Q1. Business Name Q2. Address Q3. Point of Contract (Name, Title) Q4. Phone Number Q5. Email Address Q6. Unique Entity ID Q7. Cage Code Q8. Socioeconomic Status (Other Than Small, Small, 8(a), SDVOSB, etc.) Q9. Participating Role (Prime Contractor, Subcontractor, Design Firm, Other) Other Transaction Authority (OTA) & Statutory Compliance: Q10. OTA Experience � Describe your firm�s previous experience, if any, executing projects utilizing OTA. Q11. What project characteristics make PDB OTA particularly advantageous or disadvantageous for this requirement? Progressive Design-Build (PDB) / Early Contractor Involvement: Q12. What minimum level of detail (e.g., Statement of Need, conceptual site plans, target budget) does your firm require prior to entering Phase 1 (Design/Pre-construction) to feel confident in the project's viability? Q13. What collaborative mechanisms (such as joint design charrettes, target-value design workshops, or phased scoping approvals) do you recommend the Government implement in the first 30-90 days to rapidly transition from a "blank page" to a mutually agreed-upon baseline? Q14. Describe your experience executing Progressive Design-Build, Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR), or other highly collaborative delivery methods where designer and builder worked collaboratively with the owner before locking in a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). Feedback on the Acquisition Strategy & Alternatives: Q15. Does the proposed PDB-OTA strategy incentivize your firm to participate? Why or why not? Q16. Are there alternative acquisition strategies, commercial phasing arrangements, or risk-sharing terms that the Government has not considered that would yield a higher quality facility, faster delivery, or lower cost? Bonding Capability: Q17. Specify your maximum bonding (single and aggregate) as a sole prime contractor and/or as a joint venture. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: Please submit your responses by 30 November 2026 at 1000 Eastern Standard Time (EST) to Mr. Terry Agena at terry.agena.1@us.af.mil and MSgt Quortez Dorsey quortez.dorsey@us.af.mil. The Government welcomes candid industry feedback and recommendations regarding commercial practices, agreement terms, project phasing, risk sharing, governance, pricing approaches, and other considerations that could improve successful execution of these projects under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Interested firms are encouraged to add themselves to the Interested Vendors List associated with this announcement on SAM.gov to receive future updates. Note: Do not submit proprietary trade secrets, protected technologies, or classified information in your response. All feedback received will be handled as public market research to shape the Government's final acquisition approach.

The 409th Contracting Support Brigade, Theater Contracting Command (TCC) Kleber Kaserne, Kaiserslautern, Germany, has a requirement for instructional (secondary, post-secondary, credit and non-credit) programs and education support services under NAICS 611310 at various European locations Belgium, Bulgaria, Germany, Italy, The Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Spain, Turkey, and The United Kingdom. These programs form critical elements of the adult education, voluntary education programs which support lifelong learning by Service members and other authorized adult learners within the U.S. military communities; served by the voluntary education organizations of each of the U.S. Forces in the European theater. The voluntary education programs of the U.S. Forces in Europe have as their common mission the delivery and management of the widest range possible of high-quality adult and continuing education programs normally available to the general public within the continental United States (CONUS). title: RFP-797-FSS-04-0001-R3: 621II Medical Laboratory Testing & Analysis Services
description: Revised Language SCOPE OF SOLICITATION The Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) program is also known as the GSA Schedules Program or the Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) Program. The FSS program is directed and managed by GSA and provides Federal agencies with a simplified process for obtaining commercial supplies and services at prices associated with volume buying. Indefinite-delivery, indefinite quantity contracts are awarded to provide supplies and services at stated prices for given periods of time. GSA has delegated authority to the VA to manage the Schedules for medical supplies under the VA FSS program. This solicitation is for the offering of reference laboratory services for the purpose of providing medical laboratory testing for the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of a disease or condition and to assess patient health to make clinical decisions for patient care.� This solicitation is not for facilities that only collect and/or prepare specimens nor for those facilities that only serve as a mailing service and do not perform testing services. This solicitation is issued to establish contracts which may be used on a nonmandatory basis by eligible users, as a source of supply for the supplies or services described herein, for domestic. Domestic delivery is defined as delivery within the 48 contiguous states, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Washington, DC, and U.S. territories . Offerors may be limited to geographic service areas based upon licensing requirements or may offer nationwide delivery. This solicitation further requires that offered prices cover delivery to destinations (i.e. F.O.B. destination) located within the 48 contiguous states and the District of Columbia. Offerors can choose whether or not prices cover delivery f.o.b. destination to Alaska, Hawaii, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Additionally, the solicitation defines the number of calendar days after receipt of order (ARO) within which delivery must be made. Offerors who cannot provide the required minimum geographic coverage, that is one state, will not be considered for award. As specified in the solicitation, offerors shall comply with all state, federal and local regulations, licenses, permits, and accreditation necessary to manage and conduct preanalytic specimen testing services. Offerors must comply with states that require out of state licenses/permits. Therefore, laboratories conducting clinical testing on specimens originating in a state that requires an out of state license/permit must hold that state s Department of Health (or other governing body) clinical laboratory permit, licenses, etc. � Offerors that are not compliant with the originating state s licensing and/or permit requirement, regardless of location, will not be considered for an award for that specific state. Offerors may not subcontract to another laboratory to circumvent the originating state s requirement for licensing, permits, etc. The offeror, in itself, is required to meet the requirements of the solicitation without the aid of a subcontractor. The Government retains sole discretion to determine the offeror s capability, compliance, and to limit SINs or geographic coverage. Special Item Numbers (SINs): FSS solicitations set forth broad categories of accepted products/services, referred to as Special Item Numbers (SINs), listed in the Continuation of SF1449 in Vendor Response Document 02. Offerors are not required to submit their entire catalog of products/services but are free to choose which items they will offer as long as those items fall within one of the solicitation s pre-defined SIN categories. Items that do not fall within one of these SINs are considered to be out of scope of the solicitation and cannot be awarded. An item s acceptability under the schedule may be further restricted by a determination of fair and reasonable pricing. Offered diagnostic testing services must be categorized under the accepted services referenced under the Special Item Numbers (SINs) and classified as a specialties or subspecialties of tests as defined under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA). Please note that items offered are further restricted to those tests with CPT codes. Additionally, FSS will not award any home diagnostic tests under this schedule. Home diagnostic tests/test kits may be proposed under Schedule 65 V II Invitro Diagnostics, Reagents, Test Kits and Test Sets. FDA Regulatory Requirements Reagents used to perform the tests must be FDA cleared, as appropriate, or be identified as a Laboratory Developed Test (LDT). Offerors of tests not in compliance with these requirements shall not be considered for award under this solicitation. New Items vs. Refurbished or Grey Market Goods This solicitation is for the award of new items only. The Contractor shall provide only new equipment and new parts for the required products described herein. Absolutely no grey market goods or refurbished products shall be provided under any delivery order. Grey market goods are defined as genuine branded goods sold outside of an authorized sales-territory (or by non-authorized dealers in an authorized territory) at prices lower than being charged in authorized sales territories (or by authorized dealers). All equipment must be covered by the manufacturer s warranty. Trade Agreements Act The Trade Agreements Act is applicable to all Schedules. In exercising its authority under FAR Part 25, Foreign Acquisition, purchases by Ordering Activities are restricted to either U.S.-made or designated country end products as defined in clause FAR 52.225-5. For the purposes of this services schedule, origin is determined by the country in which the firm providing the service is established, not the location at which the services are performed. For more information on these potential, additional requirements, please see the note in Solicitation Document 01 after FAR clause 52.216-18 Ordering. title: Request for Information - Contract Writing System Recompete
description: Request for Information Contract Writing System Recompete 2099AC27N00004 RFI-DO-27-002 The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to identify capable vendors and commercially available solutions that can support the U.S. Department of the Treasury requirements for a contract writing system as part of the Contract Writing System Recompete. The Government seeks information regarding vendors� technical capabilities, available products and services, hosting, system functionality, integration, and ability to satisfy the attached Technical Exhibit 1 - Contract Writing System Requirements. Interested vendors should review the entire Technical Exhibit and identify capabilities, limitations, and potential alternatives. This RFI is solely for market research and acquisition planning and is not a solicitation. This is an RFI for market research purposes, and not a solicitation. 1. SCOPE SUMMARY (See attached Technical Exhibit 1 - Contract Writing System Requirements) The Department of the Treasury is conducting market research to identify qualified vendors capable of providing an enterprise contract writing system solution to support Treasury acquisition and procurement operations. Technical Exhibit 1 identifies anticipated functional, technical, operational, security, hosting, integration, and support requirements designated as Mandatory or Value Added. The Government may use information obtained through this RFI to refine requirements and determine an appropriate acquisition strategy for any future solicitation. The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to gather information from interested vendors regarding their capabilities and potential solutions for a Contract Writing System to support the Department of the Treasury's acquisition and contracting requirements. The incumbent contractor providing the Department's existing Contract Writing System is Unison Software, Inc. II. ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE The anticipated period of performance for any resulting contract has not been finalized. Additional information regarding the period of performance, implementation schedule, and other acquisition details may be provided in a future solicitation, should one be issued. III. POTENTIAL INDUSTRY DAY / PRODUCT DEMONSTRATIONS The Government may elect to conduct an Industry Day and/or schedule individual vendor demonstrations as part of its market research efforts to better understand available commercial contract writing systems, products, solutions, services, and capabilities relevant to this RFI and the attached Technical Exhibit 1 - Contract Writing System Requirements. Interested vendors may be invited to demonstrate their proposed solutions, highlight key features and functionality, and discuss how their offerings could address the Government's operational and technical needs. Participation in any Industry Day or vendor demonstration will be voluntary and at the Government's sole discretion. Additional information regarding scheduling, format, and participation requirements will be provided if the Government determines that such an event would be beneficial. The Government is under no obligation to conduct an Industry Day or vendor demonstrations. Any such activities will be conducted solely for market research and informational purposes and will not constitute a formal evaluation of offers or quotations. Participation or nonparticipation will not guarantee or preclude consideration for, or award of, any future contract. IV. ADDITIONAL DETAILS NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE. A request for more information, or a copy of the solicitation, will not be considered an affirmative response to this Request for Information. Telephone responses or inquiries to this Request for Information will NOT be accepted. Treasury Common Services Center (TCSC) will consider responses received no later than 10:00 AM ET, November 30, 2026, as submitted in writing to chad.gambrill@treasury.gov and paul.white2@treasury.gov. Please include �RFI: 2099AC27N00004, Contract Writing System Recompete- CG/PW� in the subject line. The Government is conducting market research to identify capable vendors and commercially available solutions. Quotations and formal proposals will not be accepted at this time. The Government may, at its discretion, request clarification or additional technical information from responding vendors or conduct discussions associated with a potential Industry Day or vendor demonstration. Qualified contractors must provide the following: 1. The name and location of your company, contact information, and identify your business size and socioeconomic category. Please ensure contact information includes the name of the point of contact, email address, and telephone number should the Government have questions regarding individual responses. 2. The GSA contract or other vehicle your services are available through, including the schedule/GWAC number, NAICS Codes, and applicable SIN. 3. Capability Statement: Responding vendors shall provide a general capabilities statement describing their company, relevant experience, available contract writing system solutions, and technical capabilities. Responses should address the functional, technical, operational, hosting, integration, security, and support requirements identified in Technical Exhibit 1. 4. Technical Exhibit Response: Vendors are requested to complete the attached Technical Exhibit 1 - Contract Writing System Requirements. For each applicable requirement, indicate whether the proposed solution meets the requirement in the "Meets (Y/N)" column and provide explanatory information in the "Comments" column, as appropriate. For requirements not fully met, identify limitations, alternatives, or other approaches. Address both Mandatory and Value Added requirements. The following file extensions are not allowable and application materials/data submitted with these extensions cannot be considered: .bat, .cmd, .com, .exe, .pif, .rar, .scr, .vbs, .hta,, .cpl, and .zip files. Microsoft Office compatible documents are acceptable. Additional information regarding this RFI, including any potential Industry Day or vendor demonstrations, may be provided at the Government discretion. This notice does not restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. All firms responding to this notice are advised that their response is not a request that will be considered for contract award. All interested parties are required to respond to any resultant solicitation separately from their response to this notice, should one be issued.

description: NO PROPOSALS OR QUOTATIONS ARE REQUESTED AT THIS TIME. THIS PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. Brief Description of Services: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 2, on behalf of Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 2 South, intends to issue an RFP - Requirements Contract for comprehensive Reference Laboratory and Esoteric Testing Services. The contract will serve the VA Medical Centers listed in Appendix A. The contractor must provide everything needed to perform all required reference and esoteric laboratory testing. Peters VA Medical Center VA New Jersey Healthcare System VA Hudson Valley Healthcare System VA New York Harbor Healthcare System Northport VA Medical Center Set-Aside: Unrestricted, this is not Set-Aside. title: USAC RFP: Enterprise Data Platform
description: Update: Proposal due date extened to November 30, 2026, at 11:00 AM ET. At the request of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Office of Managing Director (OMD), and to ensure wide exposure of the Universal Service Administrative Company's (USAC) solicitations, the FCC is alerting the public that USAC has posted this solicitation on its website. The purpose of this Request for Proposal (�RFP�) is to acquire an Enterprise Data Platform. This Request for Proposals (RFP) describes the services being requested and provides instructions on how to respond. Proposals are due no later than November 23, 2026, at 11:00 AM ET. This Request for Proposals (RFP) describes the services being requested and provides instructions on how to respond. Further details provided herein. Proposals shall be submitted no later than November 23, 2026, at 11:00 AM ET. The RFP is available electronically at http://www.usac.org/about/procurement. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation issued in accordance with Part 13 of Title 48 of the Code of Federal Regulations (known as the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR)). This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; no separate written solicitation will be issued. The solicitation number is IT-26-148. Proposals are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. No additional notification will be issued by the FCC. ALL COMMUNICATIONS IN REFERENCE TO THESE OPPORTUNITIES SHALL BE THROUGH USAC'S Contracting Office. The RFP describes the services requested and provides instructions on how to respond. BACKGROUND: USAC is a not-for-profit Delaware corporation. The FCC has appointed USAC as the permanent administrator of the Universal Service Fund (USF) and the universal service support mechanisms (Support Mechanisms): High Cost (HC), Lifeline (LI), Rural Health Care (RHC) and Schools & Libraries (SL) as set forth in Title 47, Part 54, Section 701 of the Code of Federal Regulations. As part of its administrative function, USAC performs, subject to FCC oversight, the billing, collection, and disbursement functions associated with the USF and the Support Mechanisms. Additional information concerning USAC and its administration of the USF and Support Mechanisms can be obtained from USAC's website located at: www.usac.org. The purpose of this Request for Proposal (�RFP�) is to acquire an Enterprise Data Platform. This Request for Proposals (RFP) describes the services being requested and provides instructions on how to respond. Proposals are due no later than November 23, 2026, at 11:00 AM ET. The RFP is available electronically at http://www.usac.org/about/procurement. THIS IS NOT A PROCUREMENT BY A FEDERAL AGENCY, GOVERNMENT CORPORATION, GOVERNMENT CONTROLLED CORPORATION OR OTHER ESTABLISHMENT IN THE EXECUTIVE BRANCH OF THE UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT. THE CONTRACT AWARDED AS A RESULT OF THIS RFP WILL NOT BE A SUBCONTRACT UNDER A FEDERAL PRIME CONTRACT TO USAC.

title: 19WA8026Q0036 - Janitorial services at Embassy office building and Warehouse.
description: Please note this solicitation is not ready to be issued as of this date. The Embassy of the United States in Windhoek will launch the solicitation on the SAM.gov website when it is available. The U.S. Embassy in Windhoek hereby provides the following pre-solicitation notice in respect of the issuance of a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for: Janitorial/cleaning services at the U.S. Embassy Office building and General services warehouse in Windhoek, Namibia. The Contractor shall perform janitorial services in all designated spaces including, but not limited to halls, offices, restrooms, work areas, entrance ways, lobbies, storage areas, elevators, and stairways. The anticipated performance period is for a base year, with four one-year option periods, if exercised by the Government. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, which will be considered. The U.S. Government may award the contract, based on the initial offer, without any discussions. The resultant contract will be a fixed priced type of contract for its duration. The Government is planning a pre-quotation conference and the date for this conference will be in the solicitation. All contractors must be registered in the SAM (System for Award Management) Database https://www.sam.gov prior to submitting an offer pursuant to FAR provision 52.204-7. Therefore, prospective offerors are encouraged to register prior to the submittal of quotations/proposals. This opportunity is subject to 52.229-12 - Tax on Certain Foreign Procurements (FEB 2021) Electronic Submission/Responses: This opportunity allows for electronic responses. Please submit your offer prior to the response date and time. Please ensure your email with your offer does not exceed 15 MB, if it does then you might have to send more than one email. Alternatively, offers may be submitted at the US Embassy offices at the following address: 38 Metje Street, Klein Windhoek, Windhoek, Namibia.

title: Mid-Bay James Island Restoration Phase 2
description: This Invitation for Bid (IFB) solicitation is for the restoration work at James Island, Dorchester County, Maryland. James Island is an ecosystem restoration project (part of the Mid-Chesapeake Bay Island Ecosystem Restoration project, commonly referred to as Mid-Bay) located in the middle Chesapeake Bay in Dorchester County, Maryland, approximately 56 miles south-southeast of the Port of Baltimore and one mile north of Taylors Island. **Amendment 0001, dated 29 October 2026, The purpose of this amendment is to provide the James Island Phase 2 plans, and provide revisions to the CLINs structure in section 00 10 00. Bidders are encouraged to utilize the bid schedule provided in the list of attachments in lieu of the bid schedule provided in section 00 10 00. Please note, the awardee of this action will not be permitted to mobilize before 15 September 2027, per the formal Notice to Proceed. All other terms and conditions of this solicitation remain unchanged.***
